text: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end error recovery and flow control?
explanation: The Transport layer (Layer 4) provides end-to-end services including error recovery via TCP acknowledgments and flow control via TCP windowing. Data Link (Layer 2) only handles hop-to-hop error detection within a single network segment.

text: Which OSI layer encapsulates data into frames?
explanation: The Data Link layer (Layer 2) takes packets from the Network layer and encapsulates them into frames, adding a header with source/destination MAC addresses and a trailer with an FCS for error detection.

text: A network engineer captures a PDU that contains source and destination MAC addresses, an EtherType field, and an FCS. At which OSI layer does this PDU exist?
explanation: The PDU at Layer 2 (Data Link) is called a frame. It contains MAC addresses, an EtherType field identifying the Layer 3 protocol, data payload, and an FCS (Frame Check Sequence) trailer for error detection.

text: Which two layers of the OSI model does the TCP/IP model's 'Internet' layer map to? (Choose two)
explanation: The TCP/IP Internet layer maps only to the Network layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model, handling logical addressing and routing with IP. The TCP/IP Network Access layer covers OSI Layers 1 and 2 (Physical and Data Link).

text: What is the size of an IPv4 address?
explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long, typically written in dotted-decimal notation as four 8-bit octets (e.g., 192.168.1.1). IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses. MAC addresses are 48 bits.

text: What is the subnet mask for a /26 prefix?
explanation: A /26 prefix means 26 bits are network bits. The last octet has 2 host bits set: 11000000 in binary = 192. So the full mask is 255.255.255.192. This gives 64 addresses per subnet (62 usable).

text: A host has IP address 172.16.45.200/27. What is the broadcast address of its subnet?
explanation: /27 = 255.255.255.224. Block size is 32. Starting from 0: subnets are .0, .32, .64, .96, .128, .160, .192, .224. The host .200 falls in the .192 subnet (.192 to .223). Broadcast = .223.

text: Which address class was originally assigned to the range 192.0.0.0 to 223.255.255.255?
explanation: Class C addresses start with the binary prefix 110, covering 192.0.0.0–223.255.255.255. They have a default /24 mask. Class A (1–126), Class B (128–191), Class D (224–239, multicast).

text: Which protocol uses a three-way handshake to establish a connection?
explanation: TCP uses a three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) to establish a reliable connection before data transfer. UDP is connectionless and sends data without a handshake, making it faster but unreliable.

text: A web server listens on TCP port 443. What protocol is typically used on this port?
explanation: TCP port 443 is the well-known port for HTTPS (HTTP Secure), which encrypts web traffic using TLS/SSL. HTTP uses port 80, FTP uses 20/21, and SSH uses port 22.

text: Which field in the TCP header is used for flow control?
explanation: The TCP Window Size field advertises how many bytes the receiver can accept before requiring an acknowledgment, implementing flow control. If the window is full, the sender must stop and wait for an ACK.

text: What does ARP resolve?
options: A. Domain names to IP addresses
B. IP addresses to MAC addresses
C. MAC addresses to IP addresses
D. Port numbers to service names
explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) resolves IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses. When a host knows the destination IP but not its MAC, it broadcasts an ARP request; the owner of that IP replies with its MAC.

text: Which statement about IPv6 is true?
options: B. IPv6 requires NAT to communicate with IPv4
C. IPv6 uses NDP instead of ARP for address resolution
D. IPv6 still uses broadcast for neighbor discovery
explanation: IPv6 replaces ARP with NDP (Neighbor Discovery Protocol), which uses ICMPv6 multicast messages instead of broadcasts. IPv6 addresses are 128 bits. IPv6 doesn't use broadcasts at all.

text: A host sends a packet to 8.8.8.8. It knows the default gateway is 192.168.1.1. What MAC address does it put in the destination MAC field of the Ethernet frame?
options: C. The MAC of the default gateway
explanation: When sending to a remote destination, the host puts the destination IP as 8.8.8.8 but the destination MAC as the gateway's MAC. The gateway (router) then strips the frame and forwards the packet. The IP address never changes; only the MAC reframes hop-to-hop.

text: What type of cable is used to connect two switches using their standard Ethernet ports (non-Auto-MDIX)?
explanation: Connecting two like devices (switch-to-switch, PC-to-PC) traditionally requires a crossover cable, which swaps the transmit and receive pairs. Auto-MDIX on modern Cisco switches eliminates this requirement automatically.

text: Single-mode fiber is preferred over multimode fiber when the cable run exceeds approximately how many meters?
explanation: Multimode fiber supports runs up to about 550 m for 10GbE. Single-mode fiber, with its narrower core and laser light source, supports runs from 2 km to 100+ km. For campus building-to-building runs beyond ~550 m, single-mode is used.

text: Which wireless standard operates in the 5 GHz band only and supports a maximum throughput of 54 Mbps?
explanation: 802.11a operates exclusively in the 5 GHz band with max 54 Mbps. 802.11b and 802.11g operate in 2.4 GHz (11 Mbps and 54 Mbps respectively). 802.11n operates in both bands with much higher throughput.

text: Which 802.11 standard introduced MIMO and dual-band (2.4/5 GHz) support?
explanation: 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4) introduced MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) antennas and dual-band operation in both 2.4 and 5 GHz. It supports throughput up to 600 Mbps. 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) operates only in 5 GHz with MU-MIMO.

text: Which switching method reads only the destination MAC address before forwarding a frame?
explanation: Cut-through switching reads only the first 6 bytes (destination MAC) before starting to forward, minimizing latency. Store-and-forward reads the entire frame including FCS for error checking. Fragment-free reads the first 64 bytes to avoid runts.

text: A switch receives a frame with a destination MAC address not in its MAC address table. What does it do?
options: B. Sends the frame back to the source
C. Floods the frame out all ports except the one it arrived on
D. Sends an ARP request to find the destination
explanation: When a switch receives a frame with an unknown unicast destination MAC, it floods (forwards) it out all ports except the ingress port. This is called unknown unicast flooding. The switch learns MAC addresses only from source MAC addresses in incoming frames.

text: What is the primary purpose of a collision domain?
options: A. A group of devices that share the same VLAN
B. A group of devices in which a frame sent by one device can collide with a frame sent by another device
C. A group of devices that share the same IP subnet
D. A group of devices separated by a router
explanation: A collision domain is a network segment where data packets can collide. In a hub-based network, all devices share one collision domain. Each switch port creates a separate collision domain, eliminating collisions on full-duplex links.

text: Which device separates broadcast domains?
explanation: Routers separate broadcast domains. Each router interface connects to a different network, and routers do not forward broadcasts between interfaces. Switches and bridges separate collision domains but not broadcast domains (unless VLANs are configured).

text: Which private IPv4 address range is summarized as 10.0.0.0/8?
How many usable host addresses are in a /29 subnet?
explanation: /29 = 255.255.255.248. This gives 2^3 = 8 addresses per subnet. Subtract the network and broadcast addresses = 6 usable hosts. Common use: point-to-point links where /30 (2 hosts) isn't enough.

text: Which command displays the IPv4 address, subnet mask, and default gateway configured on a Windows PC?
explanation: On Windows, 'ipconfig /all' displays detailed IP configuration including IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, DNS servers, and MAC address. 'show ip interface brief' is a Cisco IOS command. 'ifconfig -a' is used on Linux/macOS.

text: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets between different networks?
explanation: The Network layer (Layer 3) uses logical addressing (IP) to route packets between networks. Routers operate at this layer.

text: What is the PDU name at the Transport layer?
explanation: Transport layer PDUs are called segments (TCP) or datagrams (UDP). Network layer PDUs are packets, Data Link are frames, Physical are bits.

text: A host sends a broadcast frame with destination MAC FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF. Which devices will process this frame?
options: B. All devices in the same VLAN
C. All devices on the internet
D. Only devices with a matching IP
explanation: Ethernet broadcasts (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) are delivered to all devices in the same broadcast domain (VLAN). Routers do not forward broadcast frames between VLANs.

text: Which TCP mechanism prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver?
explanation: TCP flow control uses a sliding window. The receiver advertises a window size that limits how much data the sender can transmit before receiving an acknowledgment.

text: Which protocol uses a three-way handshake to establish a connection?
explanation: TCP uses SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK to establish a reliable, full-duplex connection before data is exchanged. UDP is connectionless and has no handshake.

text: A web server listens on port 443. What protocol is typically used?
explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) uses TLS/SSL encryption and runs on TCP port 443. Standard HTTP uses port 80.

text: Which well-known port does DNS use?
explanation: DNS uses UDP port 53 for standard queries and TCP port 53 for zone transfers or large responses.

text: How many usable host addresses exist in a /28 subnet?
explanation: A /28 mask has 4 host bits: 2^4=16 addresses, minus 2 (network and broadcast) = 14 usable hosts.

text: What is the subnet mask in dotted-decimal for a /26 prefix?
explanation: /26 means 26 bits are 1s. The last octet has the top 2 bits set: 11000000 = 192. So the mask is 255.255.255.192.

text: A host has IP 172.16.45.100/20. What is the network address?
Which IPv6 address type is equivalent to an IPv4 private address and is only routable within a site?
explanation: Unique local addresses (FC00::/7) are IPv6's equivalent of RFC 1918 private addresses — routable within an organization but not on the internet.

text: Which IPv6 address is automatically assigned to every IPv6-enabled interface and starts with FE80::/10?
explanation: Link-local addresses (FE80::/10) are automatically configured on every IPv6 interface using EUI-64 or random generation. They are only valid on the local link.

text: What does IPv6 use instead of ARP to resolve link-layer addresses?
explanation: IPv6 replaces ARP with NDP (Neighbor Discovery Protocol), which uses ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation and Neighbor Advertisement messages to resolve MAC addresses.

text: Which type of Ethernet address identifies a specific group of hosts?
explanation: Multicast addresses identify a group of hosts. The least-significant bit of the first byte is 1 for multicast. Broadcast (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF) targets all hosts; unicast targets one.

text: Which cable standard supports 10 Gbps over distances up to 100 meters?
explanation: Cat6A (Augmented Category 6) supports 10GBASE-T at up to 100m. Cat6 can do 10 Gbps but only up to 55m. Cat5e supports 1 Gbps at 100m.

text: A network uses single-mode fiber. What is the primary advantage over multimode fiber?
explanation: Single-mode fiber (SMF) uses a narrower core and laser light to support distances of tens of kilometers. Multimode fiber (MMF) is cheaper but limited to hundreds of meters.

text: A host sends data to another host on the same subnet. Which device forwards the frame?
explanation: On the same subnet, communication happens at Layer 2. A Layer 2 switch forwards frames based on MAC address tables within the same VLAN without routing.

text: What does a switch do when it receives a frame with an unknown destination MAC address?
options: C. Floods the frame out all ports except the ingress port
D. Forwards it to the default gateway
explanation: When a switch has no entry for a destination MAC in its CAM table, it floods (unknown unicast flooding) the frame out all ports in the same VLAN except the port it arrived on.

text: What field in an Ethernet frame is used by a switch to make forwarding decisions?
explanation: Layer 2 switches make forwarding decisions based on the destination MAC address, looking it up in the MAC address table (CAM table).

text: Which field in the IP header is decremented by 1 at each router hop and causes the packet to be dropped when it reaches 0?
explanation: The TTL (Time To Live) field prevents packets from looping forever. Each router decrements TTL by 1; when it hits 0, the packet is dropped and an ICMP Time Exceeded message is sent to the source.

text: Which layer of the TCP/IP model corresponds to the OSI Physical and Data Link layers?
explanation: The TCP/IP model's Network Access (Link) layer encompasses the functions of both the OSI Physical layer (bits/signals) and Data Link layer (frames/MAC addresses).

text: Which of the following is a valid summarization of 10.0.0.0/24 through 10.0.3.0/24?
explanation: 10.0.0.0 to 10.0.3.255 spans 4 /24 networks. 4 = 2^2, so borrow 2 bits from the third octet: /24-2 = /22. The summary is 10.0.0.0/22.

text: An IPv6 address is written as 2001:0DB8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001. What is the compressed form?
explanation: IPv6 compression rules: (1) drop leading zeros in each group, (2) replace the longest run of consecutive all-zero groups with ::. Result: 2001:DB8::1.

text: Which protocol does a host use to discover the MAC address of a device on the same subnet?
explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) maps a known IPv4 address to an unknown MAC address. The host broadcasts an ARP request; the target responds with its MAC address.

text: Which wireless standard operates in both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands and supports a maximum data rate of 600 Mbps?
explanation: 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4) operates in both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz and introduced MIMO, supporting up to 600 Mbps. 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) is 5 GHz only and supports multi-user MIMO.

text: What does CSMA/CA stand for and where is it used?
options: A. Carrier Sense Multiple Access / Collision Avoidance — wireless
B. Carrier Sense Multiple Access / Collision Detection — Ethernet
C. Channel Switching Multiple Access — fiber
D. Carrier Sense Multiple Access / Collision Avoidance — coax Ethernet
explanation: CSMA/CA (Collision Avoidance) is used in 802.11 wireless networks. Devices sense the channel and use random backoff timers to avoid collisions. Ethernet uses CSMA/CD (Detection).

text: Which 802.11 band is most prone to interference from microwave ovens and cordless phones?
explanation: The 2.4 GHz band has only 3 non-overlapping channels and is heavily congested. Microwave ovens and many cordless phones also operate in this band, causing interference.

text: How many /27 subnets can be created from a single /24 network?
explanation: A /24 has 8 bits for hosts. A /27 uses 5 host bits (32-27=5), leaving 3 bits for subnets: 2^3 = 8 subnets.

text: Which protocol provides unreliable, connectionless delivery of datagrams?
explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) provides best-effort, connectionless delivery. It has no handshake, no guaranteed delivery, and no ordering. Useful for DNS, DHCP, streaming, and VoIP.

text: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for data encryption and translation between different data formats?
explanation: The Presentation layer (Layer 6) handles data translation, encryption/decryption, and compression. It ensures data from the Application layer is in a format the receiving system can use.

text: Which prefix length is used for an IPv6 loopback address?
explanation: The IPv6 loopback address is ::1/128. The /128 prefix means it's a single host address, equivalent to IPv4's 127.0.0.1/32.

text: A company needs 50 host addresses in a subnet. What is the smallest subnet mask that satisfies this requirement?
explanation: /26 gives 64 addresses (2^6), minus 2 = 62 usable hosts. /27 gives only 30 usable hosts, which isn't enough.

text: Which device operates at OSI Layer 1 and simply repeats electrical signals?
explanation: A hub is a Layer 1 device that repeats signals to all ports, creating a single collision domain. Switches (Layer 2) make intelligent forwarding decisions based on MAC addresses.

text: What is the primary purpose of the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP)?
options: B. To prevent routing loops in Layer 3 networks
C. To prevent loops in Layer 2 switched networks
D. To provide QoS for real-time traffic
explanation: STP (IEEE 802.1D) prevents Layer 2 loops in networks with redundant switch paths by placing certain ports in a blocking state.

text: Which fiber connector type is most commonly used in enterprise Ethernet deployments?
explanation: LC (Lucent Connector) is the most prevalent in modern enterprise deployments due to its small form factor. SC connectors are push-pull and also common in older installations.

text: What mechanism does TCP use to detect and recover from lost segments?
explanation: TCP uses PAR (Positive Acknowledgment with Retransmission). If the sender doesn't receive an ACK within the retransmission timer (RTO), it retransmits the unacknowledged segment.

text: Which address is the all-routers IPv6 multicast address?
explanation: FF02::2 is the all-routers multicast address. FF02::1 is all-nodes. FF02::5 is all OSPF routers, FF02::6 is OSPF DR/BDR.

text: Which address does a switch use to forward a unicast frame to the correct port?
explanation: Switches use the destination MAC address to look up the outgoing port in the CAM table. The source MAC is used to learn and populate the table.

text: Which class of IPv4 address has the first octet range of 192–223?
explanation: Class C: 192–223 in the first octet, /24 default mask, supports 254 hosts per network. Class D (224–239) is multicast, Class E (240–255) is experimental.

text: Which ICMP message type is used by the ping command to test connectivity?
options: B. Type 8 Echo Request and Type 0 Echo Reply
explanation: Ping sends ICMP Type 8 (Echo Request) and expects ICMP Type 0 (Echo Reply). Type 3 is unreachable, Type 11 is TTL exceeded (used by traceroute).

text: An 802.11ac access point is configured with channel 36 in the 5 GHz band using 80 MHz channel width. What is the maximum theoretical throughput?
explanation: 802.11ac Wave 1 with 80 MHz channel width and 1 spatial stream achieves 433 Mbps; 2 streams = 867 Mbps. 3.5 Gbps requires Wave 2 with multiple streams.

text: How long does an entry remain in a switch's MAC address table by default before aging out?
explanation: The default MAC address table aging time on Cisco switches is 300 seconds (5 minutes). Entries are refreshed each time a frame is received from that MAC address.

text: What is the broadcast address for the subnet 192.168.10.64/26?
explanation: /26 = 64 addresses per block. Starting at .64, the subnet spans .64 to .127. Network: .64, Broadcast: .127, Hosts: .65–.126.

text: Which of the following correctly describes a connection-oriented service?
options: A. Data is sent without prior negotiation
B. A virtual circuit is established before data transfer
C. Packets take different paths independently
D. No error recovery is provided
explanation: Connection-oriented services (like TCP) establish a logical connection (virtual circuit) before data exchange. This allows for guaranteed delivery, sequencing, and flow control.

text: Which IPv6 transition mechanism encapsulates IPv6 packets within IPv4 packets?
explanation: 6to4 tunneling encapsulates IPv6 packets inside IPv4 packets (protocol 41) to traverse IPv4-only infrastructure. Dual-stack runs both protocols natively. NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4.

text: Which port number is used by SNMP for trap messages sent from an agent to a manager?
explanation: SNMP uses UDP port 161 for polling (manager queries agent) and UDP port 162 for traps (agent notifies manager unsolicited). Syslog uses 514, TFTP uses 69.

text: What is the first host address in the subnet 10.10.0.0/23?
explanation: /23 spans 10.10.0.0 to 10.10.1.255 (512 addresses). Network address: 10.10.0.0, first host: 10.10.0.1, last host: 10.10.1.254, broadcast: 10.10.1.255.

text: A cable uses an RJ-45 connector. Which IEEE standard defines Gigabit Ethernet over this cable?
explanation: 1000BASE-T (IEEE 802.3ab) defines Gigabit Ethernet over Cat5e or better UTP cable using RJ-45 connectors and all 4 pairs.

text: Which protocol does a host use to automatically obtain an IPv6 address without a DHCPv6 server?
explanation: SLAAC (Stateless Address Autoconfiguration, RFC 4862) allows IPv6 hosts to generate their own addresses using the network prefix from Router Advertisements combined with an interface identifier.

text: Which OSI layer establishes, manages, and terminates sessions between applications?
explanation: The Session layer (Layer 5) manages dialog control between end systems, establishing, maintaining, and terminating sessions. Examples include NetBIOS and RPC.

text: What is the purpose of the TCP urgent pointer field?
options: B. Identifies out-of-band data that must be processed before regular data
C. Indicates the window scale factor
D. Marks the segment for fragmentation
explanation: The TCP urgent pointer identifies the end of urgent data that the receiver should process immediately, before the rest of the data stream. The URG flag must also be set.

text: A host 192.168.1.200/255.255.255.240 wants to send a packet to 192.168.1.210. Are they on the same subnet?
options: B. No — 210 is in the next subnet
C. No — 200 is the network address
D. Cannot determine without default gateway
explanation: /28 (255.255.255.240) has blocks of 16. 192.168.1.192 is the subnet containing .193–.206 as usable, with broadcast at .207. Wait — .200/28: block starting at 192 (192–207). Both 200 and 210... 210 falls in block 208–223. They are NOT on the same subnet.

text: Which type of address does a switch learn from incoming frames to populate its CAM table?
explanation: Switches learn MAC addresses dynamically by recording the source MAC address and the port number from each incoming frame. This builds the MAC address (CAM) table.

text: What is the link-local multicast address used by OSPF routers in IPv6?
explanation: FF02::5 is the all-OSPF-routers multicast address. FF02::6 is for OSPF DR/BDR. OSPFv3 for IPv6 uses these instead of the IPv4 224.0.0.5 and 224.0.0.6 addresses.

text: What does BSS stand for in 802.11 wireless networking?
explanation: BSS (Basic Service Set) consists of a single access point and all associated clients. The BSSID is the AP's MAC address. An ESS (Extended Service Set) connects multiple BSSes.

text: Which protocol is used by hosts to send error messages and operational information about IP networks?
explanation: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is used for diagnostic and error-reporting functions. Common uses include ping (echo request/reply) and traceroute (time exceeded).

text: Which of the following is an RFC 1918 private IPv4 address range?
At which OSI layer does a router primarily operate?
explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 (Network). They make forwarding decisions based on destination IP addresses and maintain routing tables. They do not use MAC addresses for forwarding.

text: What subnet does the IP address 172.20.135.200/21 belong to?
Which of the following correctly describes half-duplex communication?
options: A. Data flows in both directions simultaneously
B. Data flows in only one direction
C. Data flows in both directions but not simultaneously
D. Data flows at different speeds in each direction
explanation: Half-duplex allows bidirectional communication but only one direction at a time (like walkie-talkies). Full-duplex allows simultaneous bidirectional communication (like a phone call).

text: What is the purpose of the IPv6 anycast address?
options: A. Identify all interfaces in a group
B. Identify a single specific interface
C. Identify the nearest interface in a group
D. Identify all interfaces on a link
explanation: An anycast address is assigned to multiple interfaces, but packets are routed to the topologically nearest one. Used for services like DNS root servers.

text: Which type of UTP wiring is used to connect two similar devices directly (e.g., switch to switch)?
explanation: Crossover cables swap transmit and receive pairs, enabling direct connection of like devices (PC-to-PC, switch-to-switch). Modern switches support Auto-MDIX which detects and adjusts automatically.

text: TCP segment has SYN=1 and ACK=0. What does this indicate?
options: B. The start of a connection (first SYN in three-way handshake)
D. The server responding to a client SYN
explanation: SYN=1, ACK=0 is the first packet in TCP's three-way handshake — the client's initial connection request. The server responds with SYN=1, ACK=1.

text: A host uses EUI-64 to generate its IPv6 interface identifier. The MAC address is AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF. What is the EUI-64 interface ID?
explanation: EUI-64: insert FFFE in the middle → AABB:CCFF:FEDD:EEFF, then flip bit 7 of the first byte: AA=10101010, bit7 flip → 10101000=A8. Result: A8BB:CCFF:FEDD:EEFF.

text: What is the maximum number of non-overlapping 20 MHz channels in the 2.4 GHz band?
explanation: The 2.4 GHz band has 11 channels in North America, but only channels 1, 6, and 11 are non-overlapping with 20 MHz width. This limits co-channel interference.

text: How many IP addresses (including network and broadcast) are in a /30 subnet?
explanation: /30 has 2 host bits: 2^2 = 4 addresses total (network, 2 usable hosts, broadcast). /30 is commonly used for point-to-point links.

text: What is the function of an encapsulation process in networking?
options: A. Removing headers as data moves up the protocol stack
B. Adding headers and trailers as data moves down the protocol stack
C. Compressing data for efficient transmission
explanation: Encapsulation is the process of adding protocol headers (and sometimes trailers) at each layer as data moves from upper to lower layers. De-encapsulation removes them at the receiver.

text: Which application-layer protocol is used to transfer files and uses two TCP connections — one for control and one for data?
explanation: FTP uses TCP port 21 for control (commands) and port 20 for data transfer. TFTP uses UDP port 69 and has no authentication.

text: Which global unicast IPv6 prefix is reserved for documentation and examples?
explanation: 2001:DB8::/32 is reserved for documentation (RFC 3849). It should never appear in production routing tables. FC00::/7 is unique local, FE80::/10 is link-local.

text: A Cisco switch receives a frame on Fa0/1 with source MAC 0011.2233.4455. The CAM table shows this MAC is learned on Fa0/3. What happens?
options: B. The MAC table entry is updated to Fa0/1
C. The frame is forwarded to Fa0/3
D. A duplicate MAC alarm is triggered
explanation: When a switch receives a frame and the source MAC is already in the CAM table but from a different port, it updates the table to the new port. This handles moved devices.

text: Using VLSM, a network engineer needs: 50 hosts, 25 hosts, 10 hosts, and 2 hosts. Starting from 192.168.1.0/24, what prefix is used for the 50-host subnet?
explanation: For 50 hosts: need at least 52 addresses (50+network+broadcast). 2^6=64 ≥ 52, so /26 (255.255.255.192) works. /25 (126 hosts) wastes addresses.

text: A wireless client associates with an AP using WPA3-Personal. Which key exchange protocol does WPA3 use instead of PSK?
explanation: WPA3-Personal replaces PSK with SAE (Dragonfly handshake), which provides forward secrecy and resists offline dictionary attacks. CCMP is the encryption cipher, not the key exchange.

text: Which TCP flag is used to immediately terminate a connection without a graceful shutdown?
explanation: RST (Reset) immediately terminates a connection. FIN initiates a graceful four-way teardown. RST is used when a connection is in an inconsistent state or when rejecting a connection attempt.

text: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for converting data into electrical signals for transmission on copper cable?
explanation: The Physical layer (Layer 1) converts bits into signals (electrical, optical, or radio) for transmission on the physical medium and defines standards for cables, connectors, and signaling.

text: Which IPv6 feature allows a router to inform hosts about the network prefix and default gateway without DHCP?
explanation: Router Advertisements (ICMPv6 Type 134) are periodically sent by routers and contain prefix information, default gateway (router's link-local address), and flags indicating SLAAC or DHCPv6 use.
